newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian police find forgery shop in house attic.
newsitem.headline: Croatian police find forgery shop in house attic.

text.p: Croatian police discovered a makeshift printing shop for forging hard currency and Croatian kuna bills in a family attic in the main Adriatic port of Rijeka, the state news agency HINA reported on Wednesday.

"The discovery of the printing shop that produced U.S. dollars, German marks, Italian lira and kuna prevented an attack on Croatia's monetary system," said Zlatko Lenac, the police spokesman in the region.

Three members of a family who ran the business in their attic were arrested, HINA said. One hundred 200-kuna notes and a smaller amount of 100-dollar bills, as well as forged Croatian and foreign documents, were found in the raid.
A police official said the amount of forged notes in circulation had yet to be determined.
"It is clear that (forged) kuna notes have already circulated in Rijeka where they were discovered and withdrawn earlier," said Miljenko Vidak of the Rijeka crime squad.
